summary: Core parsing and optimization behavior looks solid, and the static build succeeds, but this should not be released yet because the actual browser UI flow is still unverified and the handoff doc overstates what was tested.
strengths: `npm test` and `npm run build` both pass, and the app remains frontend-only with a static `dist/` bundle.

Parser validation is strong: exact 10-player enforcement, duplicate-name detection, missing-cell checks, tier alias normalization, and Korean error messages are implemented in `src/lib/parseClipboard.js`.

Optimizer behavior is credible: role counts are enforced, every player is used once, deterministic tie-breaking is present, and targeted independent cross-checks matched the reported score/unranked objectives.

findings.title: Main UI flow is not actually smoke-tested
findings.detail: The only so-called UI test at `test/appFlow.test.js:8` never loads `index.html` or `src/main.js`; it just calls `buildBalanceFromClipboard()` and `render*()` helpers directly. That means the real user path in `src/main.js:15-90`—textarea input, button wiring, state transitions, reset/edit flow, and browser rendering behavior—remains unverified. Given the spec and plan require a usable paste-to-result frontend workflow and mobile/browser readiness, this is a release blocker.
findings.fix: Add a real DOM/browser smoke test that initializes the app shell, imports `src/main.js`, simulates paste and `팀 나누기`, and asserts the rendered teams/errors. If full browser automation is not possible, use a DOM-capable harness that still exercises the actual event wiring instead of pure string helpers.

findings.title: `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` overstates verification coverage
findings.detail: `FINAL_OUTPUT.md:19-20` claims `npm test` covered an integrated '붙여넣기부터 결과 렌더링까지' flow, but the current test only checks markup strings from pure functions and does not exercise the real UI entrypoint. This is misleading release documentation, especially since `FINAL_OUTPUT.md:25-26` and `:36` also acknowledge that browser-level smoke testing was not completed.
findings.fix: Either strengthen the automated test coverage so the claim becomes true, or rewrite `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` to describe the current coverage precisely and call out the remaining UI/manual QA gap without implying end-to-end verification.

required_fixes: Add a real DOM/browser smoke test for the paste -> validate -> team split -> result render workflow using the actual `src/main.js` entrypoint.
Update `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` so its verification section matches the real test scope and does not imply end-to-end UI coverage that does not exist.
verification_run: `node --input-type=module` check against `src/fixtures/samplePlayers.tsv` confirmed 2 teams of 5, role counts `1/2/2`, 10 unique players, `scoreDifference=0`, `unrankedDifference=0`, `candidateCount=113400`.
`node --input-type=module` independent optimizer cross-check across 12 random fixtures found no objective mismatches (`scoreDifference`/`unrankedDifference`).
`python3 -m http.server 4173 -d dist` failed in this sandbox with `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`, so no live browser/server smoke test evidence exists in this environment.
release_readiness: Not release-ready. The logic layer is in good shape, but the browser-facing workflow required for handoff is still unverified and the current handoff doc overclaims that coverage.
